newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest wheat futures continue to ease.
newsitem.headline: Budapest wheat futures continue to ease.

text.p: Wheat futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) continued this year's falling trend due to low demand for carry-over 1996 crops, traders said on Wednesday.
"Old (1996) wheat is still aggressively sold, and new (1997) wheat is also going down," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle Tozsdeugynoki Rt.
He added that the market was depressed by over 500,000 tonnes of 1996 wheat for which traders did not see buyers.
Milling and feed wheat futures traded on the BCE on Wednesday closed between 190 to 400 forints lower.
May milling wheat closed 190 down at 24,010 forints, while July eased 400 forints to finish at 19,200.
Corn futures traded in unusually low turnover and closed mixed. The March maturity firmed 50 forints to 17,800 while December corn dropped 300 to 18,100 forints.
Herczeg said the market took a wait-and-see attitude concerning corn, but the recent falling trend was likely to continue.
"Sellers are waiting, thinking that perhaps somebody might buy at the current high prices," he said.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
